decision_rule.statement: POINT_IN_TIME_ELIGIBLE iff every klines symbol resolves to a cap source AND no cap series carries a snapshot signature (>=2 distinct dates and >1 distinct value) AND min per-month strict breadth >= 20 AND min per-month as-of(7d) breadth >= 20.

interpretation: The committed DISP-003 panel inventory resolves to date-stamped point-in-time cap observations for every symbol, none carries a snapshot signature, and the strict same-day breadth stays above the arity requirement of 20 in every fresh-window month. The fresh-window breadth is therefore point-in-time cap-eligible. It is still a coverage/eligibility fact over a fixed panel inventory, not a proven point-in-time rank universe: rank provenance remains NOT_PROVEN_COMPLETE and today's ranks are never backfilled.
label: POINT_IN_TIME_ELIGIBLE
note: EXPLORATORY_ONLY descriptive measurement on committed development inputs. No returns, spreads, dispersion states, p-values, costs or inference computed. Does not validate, replace or unlock any confirmatory track (H1/H6/H7/H10) and is not independent confirmation. H10 remains date-gated to 2026-11-30.
question: Is the >=20 fresh-window concurrent breadth over the committed DISP-003 klines panels backed by point-in-time (historical, date-stamped, never snapshot-backfilled) cap observations, and is that inventory a proven point-in-time market-cap rank universe?

rank_provenance.label: NOT_PROVEN_COMPLETE
rank_provenance.reason: A rank requires the full eligible population on each date; the committed panel inventory is a fixed coverage set, not a proven point-in-time rank universe. universe_frontier.json records historical_rank_coverage_state=NOT_PROVEN_COMPLETE and last_verified_historical_rank=null. Today's ranks are never backfilled as historical ranks.
